# The three-valued X = Y of balls, two-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_equal_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The three-valued answer to whether $x = y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, $X$ and $Y$ not being empty, $X$ the ball of center $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y = c_{y0} + c_{y1}$ and radius $r_y$: *yes* only if it holds for every choice of members, *no* only if it fails for every choice, otherwise *unknown*, both masks false:

$$\mathit{yes} \implies X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x = y \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y, \qquad \mathit{no} \implies X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } \lnot(x = y) \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$, $c_y = c_{y0} + c_{y1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{yes}$ is true only if $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x = y \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$; $\mathit{no}$ only if $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } \lnot(x = y) \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$; never both. Both false is the answer *unknown*.
- An empty operand gives *unknown*, and so does the whole line.
- When an operand is the empty set or the whole line, the answer is exact: each mask is true exactly when its relation holds.
- For finite operands the answer may be *unknown* although one of the relations holds, close to where it stops holding: certain, not exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_equal_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallCompare2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallCompare2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_equal_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_equal_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the radii and the centers compared, and a bound of the sum of the radii with a bound of the distance of the centers (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_equal_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_equal_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`eq_2_2`](eq_2_2.md), [`add_ball_2_2`](add_ball_2_2.md), [`radd`](radd.md), [`abs_2`](abs_2.md), [`to_down_2`](to_down_2.md), [`add_up_1`](add_up_1.md).

```
# The three-valued X = Y of balls with 2-limb centers (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface",
# "Comparisons": certain): yes when both balls are the same point, r_x = r_y = 0 and c_x = c_y by
# eq_2_2, which is exact; no when the balls are disjoint, s < al, al = RD(to_down_2(abs_2(z)) - e),
# written as minus the rounding up of the opposite, a finite lower bound of |c_y - c_x|, and s =
# radd(r_x, r_y) an upper bound of r_x + r_y. Never both. Both false for an empty operand and for
# the whole line. The yes is exact; the no is certain, not exact.

ea          = eq(rx, 0)
eb          = eq(ry, 0)
ec          = eq_2_2(cx0, cx1, cy0, cy1)
eab         = and(ea, eb)
yes         = and(eab, ec)
ncx0        = neg(cx0)
ncx1        = neg(cx1)
(z0, z1, e) = add_ball_2_2(cy0, cy1, ncx0, ncx1)
s           = radd(rx, ry)
(w0, w1)    = abs_2(z0, z1)
wd          = to_down_2(w0, w1)
nw          = neg(wd)
tl          = add_up_1(e, nw)
al          = neg(tl)
aa          = abs(al)
fa          = lt(aa, const inf)
b           = lt(s, al)
no          = and(b, fa)
```
